key_insight: AI-assisted sampling identifies ten stable SrTiO₃ grain-boundary structures whose composition and reconstruction govern electronic behavior, electric fields, and local polarization.
engineering_relevance: The framework could guide oxide-perovskite interface engineering for carrier control, but the abstract does not demonstrate solar-cell performance gains.
method: Combine Grand Canonical Monte Carlo with a universal machine-learning interatomic potential to sample boundary structures and compositions.
Map chemical-potential stability and compare structural motifs across three grain boundaries.
Use density functional theory and electrostatics analysis to characterize electronic states, fields, and polarization.
evidence_signal: For Σ5(310)[001], the phase diagram identifies ten stable structures in four motif families, and DFT reveals four electronic regimes: localized electron-doped, delocalized electron-doped, insulating, and hole-attracting.
watch_item: Predictions concern selected SrTiO₃ grain boundaries; transferability to other perovskites and experimental devices remains to be validated.
paper_title: Uncovering the Structural, Electronic, and Electrostatic Landscapes of SrTiO$_3$ Grain Boundaries via Grand Canonical Monte Carlo with a Machine-Learning Interatomic Potential
